content: I also started with MCTS but then switched to ALNS

Now that everyone is publishing their solutions, I'm curious if anyone tried game theory based agents. Please share your experiences if you did, would be nice to have a chat :)

I was working on a solution based on infoset-aware Monte Carlo Tree Search and Deep CFR minimization. The action space was supposed to be abstracted to macro-level decisions like "produce N of X in T days", timed sales, etc. The idea was that Deep CFR would produce a solution that is hard to exploit and MCTS might be better at exploitation, and both could be submitted to see which one is better. I didn't make it in time because I joined the competition a bit late and the implementation of these algorithms on a new game is pretty demanding. I also made a mistake of not improving a micro-action resolver in parallel, so the solution was not competitive before the deadline mostly because the farmer and hand actions were not scheduled efficiently enough to execute top-level policy.

It's possible that inference-time CPU restriction is too debilitating for any kind of MCTS algorithm anyway, but it felt like a theoretically right fit for this game.
